# Results {#sec-results}

Results are given at three levels: the country (national forest, all forest types together), each forest type, and each forest type within each administrative region. Forest types are those observed in the field, and plots that cover several forest types are split between them (@sec-methods). The country and forest type levels are presented in this section, and the forest type and region level in Annex 2.

- **ME** is the margin of error at the 90% confidence level, as a percentage of the estimate. It is not given for domains with a single plot.
- **Plots (n)** is the number of phase 2 clusters with at least one plot section in the domain. In the non-forest domain, it includes the phase 1 points of the non-forest stratum.
- Plot counts (threatened species, wildlife, disturbance, regeneration species frequency, NTFP availability and products) use the accessible field plots, assigned to the forest type of their main LULC section.
- At forest type and region level (Annex 2), many domains have few plots and the estimates are indicative only.
- The non-forest domain is only reported for areas. For the other results, the country level is the national forest: per hectare values are per hectare of forest, totals are totals of the forest area, and plot counts use the forest plots.

## Biological Diversity

### Tree Species Composition and Diversity

<!-- IVI, Shannon index keep the top 10 or 20. We can do it by species and genus and family -->

The Importance Value Index (IVI) is the sum of the relative density, relative frequency and relative dominance (basal area) of each taxon, from 0 to 300. Density and basal area are two-phase estimates. Frequency is the number of plot sections where the taxon is recorded. Unidentified trees are not included.

The tables give the top 10 taxa by IVI, with the relative density, frequency and dominance that make up the index. The top 20 species, genera and families are in Annex 3.

The most important species at country level are shown in @fig-ivi-species and @tbl-ivi-species-country, and in each forest type in @fig-ivi-species-ftype and `r ftype_ref(tab$b_ivi_species, "ivi-species")`. Genera are in @tbl-ivi-genus-country and `r ftype_ref(tab$b_ivi_genus, "ivi-genus")`, families in @tbl-ivi-family-country and `r ftype_ref(tab$b_ivi_family, "ivi-family")`, and the Shannon index in @tbl-shannon-country, @tbl-shannon-ftype and @fig-shannon. The same tables by forest type and region are in Annex 2.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ivi-species
#| fig-cap: "Top 20 species by Importance Value Index, country level."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 5.8
fig$b_ivi_species
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ivi-species-ftype
#| fig-cap: "Top 10 species by Importance Value Index in each forest type."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 8.5
fig$b_ivi_species_ftype
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-shannon
#| fig-cap: "Shannon index of tree species by forest type and region. Error bars: 90% confidence interval."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
fig$b_shannon
```

```{r}
#| include: false
## IVI tables: IVI and its relative components only
ivi_drop <- c("n_pp", "density", "density_mep", "basal_area", "n_sections")
```

#### Importance Value Index of species

```{r}
#| results: asis
print_levels(top_n_levels(tab$b_ivi_species, 10), "ivi-species", "Top 10 species by Importance Value Index", .heading = "#####", .drop = ivi_drop, .split_ftype = TRUE)
```

#### Importance Value Index of genera

```{r}
#| results: asis
print_levels(top_n_levels(tab$b_ivi_genus, 10), "ivi-genus", "Top 10 genera by Importance Value Index", .heading = "#####", .drop = ivi_drop, .split_ftype = TRUE)
```

#### Importance Value Index of families

```{r}
#| results: asis
print_levels(top_n_levels(tab$b_ivi_family, 10), "ivi-family", "Top 10 families by Importance Value Index", .heading = "#####", .drop = ivi_drop, .split_ftype = TRUE)
```

#### Shannon diversity index

The Shannon index $H'$ is computed from the estimated density of each taxon in the domain, at species, genus and family level. Richness is the number of taxa recorded, and evenness is $H' / \ln(\text{richness})$.

```{r}
#| results: asis
print_levels(tab$b_shannon, "shannon", "Shannon diversity index", .heading = "#####")
```

### Rare, Threatened and Endangered Tree Species

<!-- Check the whole species list against the IUCN checklist. -->

Tree species are matched with the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species (version published on GBIF, `r format(info$iucn_date, "%B %Y")`). Threatened species are in the categories Critically Endangered (CR), Endangered (EN) and Vulnerable (VU). Occurrence is the number of accessible field plots with at least one live tree of the species (@fig-iucn, @tbl-iucn-country and @tbl-iucn-ftype, and by region `r annex_ref(tab$c_iucn, "iucn")` in Annex 2). The category of all recorded species is in @tbl-iucn-all.

```{r}
#| label: fig-iucn
#| fig-cap: "Number of plots with threatened tree species, by forest type."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4.3
fig$c_iucn
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
print_levels(tab$c_iucn, "iucn", "Tree species in the IUCN Red List threatened categories", .drop = "tree_iucn_category")
```

#### All recorded species

```{r}
#| results: asis
print_tab(fmt_tab(tab$c_species_iucn, .drop = "tree_iucn_category"), "IUCN Red List category of all recorded tree species. NA: not assessed or not identified to species level.", "tbl-iucn-all")
```

### Forest Regeneration

```{r}
#| include: false
regen_ctry <- tab$j_regen$country |> mutate(regen_class = as.character(regen_class)) |> split(~regen_class)
```

Seedlings (height below 1.3 m) and saplings (height of at least 1.3 m and DBH below 10 cm) of tree species are counted in the regeneration subplot of each plot, two-phase estimates (@sec-est-plot-records). At country level, the regeneration density is `r format(regen_ctry$Total$regen_ha, big.mark = ",")` individuals/ha (ME `r regen_ctry$Total$regen_mep`%), with `r format(regen_ctry$Seedlings$regen_ha, big.mark = ",")` seedlings/ha and `r format(regen_ctry$Saplings$regen_ha, big.mark = ",")` saplings/ha (@tbl-regen-country). Densities by forest type are in @fig-regen and @tbl-regen-ftype, and by forest type and region in `r annex_ref(tab$j_regen, "regen")` (Annex 2). Richness is the number of identified species recorded in the accessible field plots of the domain.

The main species of the regeneration are in @tbl-regen-species-country and @tbl-regen-species-ftype. Relative density is the share of the species in the total regeneration density of the domain, and plots with record the share of accessible field plots with at least one seedling or sapling of the species.

```{r}
#| label: fig-regen
#| fig-cap: "Density of seedlings and saplings by forest type and region. Error bars: 90% confidence interval."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
fig$j_regen
```

#### Seedlings and saplings


## Productive Functions of Forests

### Non-Timber Forest Products

```{r}
#| include: false
ntfp_ftype <- tab$k_ntfp$forest_type |> filter(ntfp_use == "Any NTFP") |> split(~forest_type)
```

NTFPs are recorded in the main plot with their use categories and their availability (few, moderate, abundant), without quantities. The share of the area with at least one NTFP is the indicator of the productive function of forests for NTFPs, two-phase estimates (@sec-est-plot-records). NTFPs are found on `r ntfp_ftype[["Closed Forest"]]$area_ntfp_pct`% of the closed forest area and `r ntfp_ftype[["Open Forest"]]$area_ntfp_pct`% of the open forest area, and were not recorded in mangrove forest (@fig-ntfp, @tbl-ntfp-country and @tbl-ntfp-ftype). Results by forest type and region are in `r annex_ref(tab$k_ntfp, "ntfp")` (Annex 2).

The accessible field plots with NTFP are counted by the highest availability recorded for each use category in @tbl-ntfp-avail-country and @tbl-ntfp-avail-ftype, and by forest type and region in `r annex_ref(tab$k_ntfp_avail, "ntfp-avail")` (Annex 2). The most frequent products are in @tbl-ntfp-product-country and @tbl-ntfp-product-ftype.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ntfp
#| fig-cap: "Share of area with NTFP by use category and forest type. Error bars: 90% confidence interval."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
fig$k_ntfp
```

#### Share of area with NTFP

```{r}
print_levels(tab$k_ntfp, "ntfp", "Share of area with NTFP, by use category", .heading = "#####")
```

### Forest Biomass and Carbon Stocks

```{r}
#| include: false
agb_ctry <- tab$i_biomass$country |> mutate(tree_group = as.character(tree_group)) |> split(~tree_group)
```

Aboveground biomass (AGB) of live trees is estimated with the allometric equation of @chave2014. AGB per hectare is the ratio estimate of the domain, and the total AGB is the AGB per hectare times the domain area. Baobabs (*Adansonia digitata*) are reported separately: their AGB is calculated with the same equation, from their measured height and wood density, but the equation is not calibrated for their water-storing stem and these values are indicative only. Each table gives the trees without baobab, the baobabs alone and all trees together.

At country level, AGB is `r format(agb_ctry[["All trees"]]$agb_ha, nsmall = 1)` t/ha for all trees (ME `r agb_ctry[["All trees"]]$agb_ha_mep`%), of which `r format(agb_ctry[["Trees without baobab"]]$agb_ha, nsmall = 1)` t/ha for trees without baobab and `r format(agb_ctry[["Baobab"]]$agb_ha, nsmall = 1)` t/ha for baobabs (@fig-biomass-ftype and @tbl-biomass-country). Results by forest type are in @fig-biomass-ftype and @tbl-biomass-ftype, and by forest type and region in @fig-biomass and `r annex_ref(tab$i_biomass, "biomass")` (Annex 2).

```{r}
#| label: fig-biomass-ftype
#| fig-cap: "Aboveground biomass of trees without baobab and of baobabs, country level and by forest type. Error bars: 90% confidence interval of all trees, n = number of plots."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
fig$i_biomass_ftype
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-biomass
#| fig-cap: "Aboveground biomass of trees without baobab and of baobabs, by forest type and region. Error bars: 90% confidence interval of all trees, n = number of plots."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4
fig$i_biomass
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
print_levels(tab$i_biomass, "biomass", "Aboveground biomass")
```

## Protective Functions of Forests

### Soil Condition and Characteristics

Soil surface condition, organic layer depth, topsoil and subsoil texture, and topsoil colour are observed at the measurement point of each plot (visual soil assessment). The shares of area in each class are two-phase estimates, using the plots with an observation of the attribute (@sec-est-plot-records). Results are given for the national forest (country level) and by forest type (@fig-soil, @tbl-soil-country and @tbl-soil-ftype). Soil results are not given by region. They describe site conditions and are not direct measures of soil fertility or degradation.

```{r}
#| label: fig-soil
#| fig-cap: "Share of area by soil class, all forest (country level) and forest types."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 5.5
fig$l_soil
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
print_levels(tab$l_soil, "soil", "Share of area by soil class")
```
